title: Electronic Structure of Atoms - Chemistry - Orbital Diagrams
subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which orbital diagram correctly represents the valence shell of Nitrogen ($N​$, $2s^2 2p^3$) according to Hund's Rule?
questions.explain: Hund's rule dictates that the three $2p$ electrons must occupy separate orbitals with parallel spins to maximize stability. Option (b) shows three unpaired electrons with the same spin orientation.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: In the ground state orbital diagram for Nickel ($Ni$, $Z=28$), how many unpaired electrons are present?
questions.explain: Nickel is $[Ar] 4s^2 3d^8$. The $d​$ subshell has 5 orbitals. With 8 electrons, 3 orbitals are filled ($3 \\times 2 = 6$) and 2 orbitals are half-filled ($2 \\times 1 = 2$). Total unpaired electrons = 2.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: An atom is **diamagnetic** if all its electrons are paired. Which of the following elements is diamagnetic in its ground state?
questions.explain: Zinc ($Zn$, $Z=30$) has the configuration $[Ar] 4s^2 3d^{10}$. Both the $s​$ and $d​$ subshells are fully filled, meaning all electrons are paired. Therefore, Zinc is diamagnetic.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which orbital diagram represents an atom in an **excited** state?
questions.explain: In option (c), the $1s$ orbital is full, but the electron that should be in the $2s$ orbital has been promoted to a higher energy $2p$ orbital. This represents an excited state.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which notation correctly represents the box diagram for the $2p^4$ subshell configuration?
questions.explain: For $p^4$ (4 electrons in 3 orbitals): First place one electron in each orbital $(\uparrow)(\uparrow)(\uparrow)$, then pair the fourth electron in the first orbital $(\uparrow\downarrow)(\uparrow)(\uparrow)$.
questions.subject: Chemistry
